problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=N\times Z$ in the Cartesian plane?
worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S=N\times Z
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is a natural number and whose $y$-coordinate is an integer number.

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in N,\,y\in Z}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any integer number.

$$
{S}_{1}={(1,y)\,:\,y\in Z}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/179fdaa3921cb29f2d25ff97bce262fd13fb2ff591c12e97a33953e95967f6fc.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{2}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $2$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any natural number.

$$
{S}_{2}={(2,y)\,:\,y\in Z}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{2}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/7399e42988df8a809013393d8873b6a6e5f60b64c0419eadd7bb3c334eb410d6.png)

We can create the subsets ${S}_{3},{S}_{4},{S}_{5},…$ similarly. Our Cartesian product $S$ is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}\cup {S}_{3}\cup … \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in N}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize $N\times Z$ as the set of points in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/16ff13c793d3c3f57eefee638fbc1ff83569ef6d084d9d053f8585f72c8812d7.png)
